title: One call, one door, three kinds of Cedar answer
lede: Simulated: a mock agent calls a tool on a mock Privilege door. Sign-in comes first, then the AI policies (Cedar) answer allowed, held for a human or refused. Pick a scenario and press Simulate; only the act.sub case has a result measured on a real tenant.

nodes.label: Tool is served
sub: allowed: every forbid was lifted or none applied

nodes.label: Call refused
sub: the message carries the policy's reason

steps.title: The agent calls a tool
steps.what: tools/call with a mock token as a Bearer. The door checks sign-in first.
steps.why: No token is refused here, before any policy (in this mock; the real door wording and checks were not measured).

steps.title: The AI policies decide
steps.what: Each Active policy on the tool is evaluated for the action the call carries: refuse (mcp:Invoke) or hold (mcp:InvokeUnattended).
steps.why: Only Active policies are enforced; per the console documentation (not re-run here, UNVERIFIED) a Candidate is not.

steps.title: A held call waits for a human
steps.what: A person approves it, approval_count becomes 1, and the retry is allowed. Simulated here.
steps.why: How the real gateway tells an unattended call apart, and what a real hold returns, were not measured (UNVERIFIED).
